newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index jumps 1.14 pct at open.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index jumps 1.14 pct at open.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index leaped forward at the start of trading on Monday morning, prompted by a strong rebound on Wall Street on Friday, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index opened with a gain of 150 points to 13,394, then rapidly advanced 191 points to 13,414.
"It's because the Dow was up 100 points on Friday," said a broker with a Singaporean house.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 101.60 points, roughly 1.6 percent, to 6,544.09 after weekly jobless claims reported on Thursday suggested that the U.S. economy is going to grow at a moderate, non-inflationary rate.
The broker said the market was also digesting the news of a corporate reshuffle by the Cheung Kong group.
Trading in index constituents Cheung Kong, Hutchison Whampoa and Hongkong Electric, as well as subsidiary Cheung Kong Infrastructure was suspended on Monday.
Hutchison plans to make a general offer for Hongkong Electric and then transfer its stake in the utility to Cheung Kong Infrastructure (CKI) in exchange for new CKI shares.

Cheung Kong will also trasnfer its existing shareholding in CKI, equal to 70.66 percent of CKI's issued capital, to Hutchison. Based on Hutchison's Friday closing price of HK$58.50 and CKI's of HK$21.15, Hutchison will pay for the CKI shares by issuing 349.50 million new shares to parent Cheung Kong.
Brokers said the deals at first glance looked good for Hutchison and not initially beneficial to CKI, but reserved judgement as they studied the new structure.
Properties led the market's rise, followed by utilities. The Hang Seng China Enterprise Index advanced only 0.37 percent to 1,062.92, but the mid cap index put on a whopping 1.06 percent.
Property related shares put on hefty gains, led by Sun Hung Kai Properties which advanced HK$1.50 to HK$95.75.
China Light rose HK$0.70 to HK$34.70 and Hongkong Telecom gained HK$0.20 to HK$12.50.
H share Tsingtao Brewery jumped HK$0.10 to HK$3.375, while mid-cap Dah Sing Financial surged HK$0.60 to HK$31.60
After 45 minutes of trade, turnover has risen to a hefty HK$2.56 billion.
